prompt: Help me untangle this mess. In my fmodel + flutter_bloc project I have a `class AddItemEvent` in my bloc file AND an `ItemAddedEvent` domain event from my decider, plus an `AddItemState` in the bloc and an `AddItemState` write-model state in my decider. My teammates can't tell which is which and code review is painful. My bloc's AddItemEvent handler currently constructs the domain ItemAddedEvent directly and I think that's wrong. Explain what each of these things actually is, tell me exactly what to rename and what to leave alone, and show the corrected bloc + state where the UI intent flows to the domain the right way. I want a rule I can apply everywhere, not just a one-off fix.
assertions: Explains the collision clearly: a bloc event is a UI intent (maps to a Command); a domain event (ItemAddedEvent) is a fact emitted by the decider.
Recommends renaming the presentation types to carry Ui markers (AddItemEvent -> AddItemUiEvent, the bloc's AddItemState -> AddItemUiState).
Explicitly says to leave the domain types unchanged (ItemAddedEvent and the decider's write-model AddItemState keep their fmodel names).
Identifies the bug: the bloc handler must build/dispatch an AddItemCommand and let the aggregate emit ItemAddedEvent; the bloc must not construct the domain event itself.
Shows a corrected bloc where the intent flows UI intent -> AddItemCommand -> service/aggregate.handle -> UiState built from the read-side projection.
States a reusable, generalizable naming rule (domain layer keeps fmodel names; every presentation type carries a Ui marker) rather than a one-off fix.
